source_text: Quid mirum, fratres dilectissimi, si oratio talis est quam Deus docuit, qui magisterio suo omnem precem nostram salutari sermone breuiauit? hoc iam per Esaiam prophetam fuerat ante praedictum, cum plenus Spiritu sancto de Dei maiestate ac pietate loqueretur. uerbum consummans, inquit, et breuians in iustitia, quoniam sermonem breuiatum faciet Deus in toto orbe terrae. nam cum Dei sermo Dominus noster Iesus Christus omnibus uenerit et colligens doctos pariter et indoctos omni sexu adque aetati praecepta salutis ediderit, praeceptorum suorum fecit grande conpendium, ut in disciplina caelesti discentium memoria non laboraret, sed quod esset simplici fidei necessarium uelociter disceret. sic cum doceret quid sit uita aeterna, sacramentum uitae magna et diuina breuitate conplexus est dicens: haec est autem uita aeterna ut cognoscant te solum et uerum Deum et quem misisti Iesum Christum. item cum de lege et prophetis praecepta prima et maiora decerperet, audi, inquit, Israel: Dominus Deus tuus Dominus unus est, et: diliges Dominum Deum tuum de toto corde tuo et de tota anima tua et de tota uirtute tua. hoc primum, et secundum simile huic: diliges proximum tuum tamquam te. in his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet et prophetae. et iterum: quaecumque uolueritis ut faciant uobis homines bona, ita et nos facite illis. haec est enim lex et prophetae.
thought_title: God's teaching shortens prayer and the law
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why the Lord's Prayer is so brief: God himself taught it, and Scripture had foretold that God would make a shortened word on the earth.
pass_a_gloss: What [is] wonderful, brothers most beloved, if [the] prayer such is which God taught, who by [his] teaching all our prayer with [a] saving word shortened? this already through Isaiah [the] prophet had been before predicted, when full [of the] Holy Spirit about [the] majesty of God and [his] piety he was speaking. [a] word completing, he says, and shortening in righteousness, since [a] word shortened will make God in [the] whole orb of [the] earth. for when [the] word of God our Lord Jesus Christ to all came and gathering [the] learned equally and [the] unlearned [of] every sex and age [the] precepts of salvation gave, [of] his precepts he made [a] great compendium, so that in [the] heavenly discipline [of] those learning [the] memory not should labor, but what was to simple faith necessary quickly [it] might learn. thus when he was teaching what is life eternal, [the] sacrament of life [with] great and divine brevity he embraced saying: this is moreover life eternal that they may know you [the] only and true God and whom you sent Jesus Christ. likewise when from [the] law and [the] prophets [the] precepts first and greater he was selecting, hear, he says, Israel: [the] Lord your God [the] Lord one is, and: you shall love [the] Lord your God from [your] whole heart and from [your] whole soul and from [your] whole strength. this [is the] first, and [the] second [is] like to this: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. in these two precepts [the] whole law hangs and [the] prophets. and again: whatever you wish that they should do to you men good [things], so also you do to them. this is for [the] law and [the] prophets.

pass_b_english: What wonder is it, dearly beloved brothers, if the prayer is such as God taught, who by his own instruction shortened all our petition in a saving word? This had already been foretold through the prophet Isaiah, when he spoke full of the Holy Spirit about the majesty and goodness of God. “A word completing and shortening in righteousness,” he says, “for God will make a shortened word in the whole circle of the earth” (Isaiah 10:22-23; cf. Romans 9:28). For when the Word of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, came to all, and gathering the learned and the unlearned together, of every sex and age, he set forth the teachings of salvation, he made a great compendium of his commandments, so that in heavenly discipline the memory of those learning should not labor, but should quickly learn what was necessary for simple faith. Thus when he taught what eternal life is, he embraced the sacrament of life with great and divine brevity, saying: “This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (John 17:3). Likewise, when he was selecting the first and greater commandments from the law and the prophets, he said: “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one Lord. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. This is the first, and the second is like it: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets hang” (Mark 12:29-31). And again: “Whatever good things you wish people to do to you, do also to them. For this is the law and the prophets” (Matthew 7:12).

problems.source_quote: uerbum consummans, inquit, et breuians in iustitia, quoniam sermonem breuiatum faciet Deus in toto orbe terrae
problems.why: The quotation is Isaiah 10:22-23 (or Romans 9:28), not Isaiah 28:16.

fixed: The quotation 'uerbum consummans... in toto orbe terrae' is Isaiah 10:22-23, not Isaiah 28:16; corrected the citation.

last_rejected.source_quote: uerbum consummans, inquit, et breuians in iustitia, quoniam sermonem breuiatum faciet Deus in toto orbe terrae
last_rejected.why: The citation Isaiah 10:22-23 is wrong; this is Isaiah 28:16 in LXX/Old Latin numbering, or more precisely the text matches Isaiah 10:22-23 in Hebrew numbering is incorrect. The verse quoted is actually Isaiah 28:16 (LXX) or the passage appears in Romans 9:28 as Pauline citation of Isaiah. The source text cites Isaiah speaking, but the modern citation should be Isaiah 28:16 or the passage as cited in Romans 9:28, not Isaiah 10:22-23.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'sermonem breuiatum faciet Deus in toto orbe terrae' matches Isaiah 10:23 (Vulgate), correctly cited; Romans 9:28 cross-ref also apt.

last_rejected.quote: the whole circle of the earth
last_rejected.why: orbis terrae means 'world' or 'earth,' not 'circle of the earth.' The phrase 'whole circle of the earth' is archaic/poetic but misleading; 'whole world' or 'whole earth' is the standard sense.
last_rejected.ruling: 'orbis terrae' literally denotes the circular world; 'circle of the earth' is an acceptable rendering within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: This is the first, and the second is like it: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets hang” (Mark 12:29-31).
last_rejected.source_quote: hoc primum, et secundum simile huic: diliges proximum tuum tamquam te. in his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet et prophetae.
last_rejected.why: “The second is like it” and “the law and the prophets hang” are Matthew 22:38-40, not Mark 12:29-31.
last_rejected.fix: Cite the composite as Mark 12:29-31 and Matthew 22:37-40.
last_rejected.ruling: The quoted text is a Mark 12/Matthew 22 conflation ("hoc primum, et secundum simile huic", "in his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet"). Cyprian combines them, so the citation is an imprecise gloss, not a mistranslation.
